newsitem.title: USA: Pa. Gov renews fight to sell liquor stores -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Pa. Gov renews fight to sell liquor stores -- paper.

text.p: Pennsylvania Gov Tom Ridge renewed his attempt to get Pennsylvania out of the liquor business, the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reported.
Ridge threatened to halt funding for capital projects such as stadiums and tourist attractions until his proposal to sell state stores has a full hearing before the legislature.

The Governor estimated that selling off the stores run by the Liquor Control Board would raise about $600 million over the next ten years. The money would be used to pay for major projects around the state.
Critics of the plan fear privatization of the liquor stores would mean an increase in alcohol sales, and weakened state control over sales to minors.
